newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate dips to 9.498 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate dips to 9.498 pct.

text.p: The Philippine benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate slipped to an average of 9.498 percent at the regular weekly auction from 9.724 percent last week, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday.
Average rates for the 182-day and 364-day bills also declined due to excess liquidity in the market. Total tenders for the three tenors reached 21.91 billion pesos.
The six-month bill rate went down to 9.842 percent from last week's 9.969 percent, while the one-year bill rate slipped to 10.388 percent from 10.517 percent.
Bids for the three-month bills totalled 8.905 billion pesos, but the auction committee accepted only one billion pesos worth of bills.
Tenders for the six-month bills reached 5.390 billion pesos, while the one-year bills attracted 7.615 billion pesos.
The auction committee awarded 1.5 billion pesos worth for the six-month bills and 2.0 billion pesos for the one-year bills.
